note: Climate portfolio comparison on the carbon model's decided package (case 'full' in build/carbon-config.json, written by index/tools/carbon-model.py during run-all.sh). Every case changes named levers against that package with identical physical assumptions. Magnitudes marked ASSUMED are planning assumptions, not scores. Nothing here is a canonical input.
residential_kwh_source: EIA FAQ 97: 10,791 kWh a year (about 899 a month) for the average residential customer, 2022

benchmarks.source: U.S. NDC submitted December 2024 (61-66% below 2005 by 2035, net zero by 2050). The U.S. withdrawal from the Paris Agreement took effect January 27, 2026; the range is used as the project's benchmark, not as a current federal commitment.

cases.cost_note: The model books no cost for industrial investment support (only the hydrogen credit), so this case's saving is understated

cases.label: Without the whole credit bundle (diagnostic only)
Public grid delivery: federal builder of last resort and reconductoring program (CLI-10 as the model's grid program, $12B a year 2030-39, ASSUMED)

Redirect test: public grid replaces the wind, solar and storage credits
Low-income heat-pump retrofits tripled (0.75 million homes a year from 2031, against 0.25 million in the package)

external_cost_bn_2025.basis: estimate: 0.5 million extra homes a year for 2031-39 at $15,000 a home ($10,000-25,000) for a heat pump with weatherization; DOE's Weatherization average-cost-per-unit limit (about $8,500 in 2025 state plans) covers shell work only

cases.cost_note: Unpriced: the model books no cost for industrial support; a contract or procurement price is needed before any cost per ton
